# Story 108 — REPORTS-4-API admin — today means today where I am, not in UTC (Story: CRM-130)

## Plan review — read this before the sections below

Reviewed 2026-09-02 against the code, every citation opened. The core reasoning
is right and unusually well argued: one window module, one refusal path, no date
library, a zone is not an offset because a zone changes offset twice a year, and
a wrong day answered confidently is worse than a refusal. **Seven things are
wrong**, and the second one changes what this story builds. Where a section
below contradicts this one, this one wins.

### 0 — There were two plans for this story, and this is the survivor.

Two ran four minutes apart, at 10:17 and 10:21. That is **L-64**, and
`verify-plan` failed on it rather than a person noticing, which is what that
check was added for.

This file is the one kept, because it carries the span ceiling and validates the
zone against a `Set` built once rather than a `try/catch` per request. **One
argument is grafted from the other and is better than this file's:** deriving
midnight has to be offset-aware and re-checked, because the offset at midnight
UTC on a date is not necessarily the offset at midnight local on that date. See
item 6.

The second one, numbered 109, is deleted. Two files for one story is a story
where somebody later reads the wrong one.

### 1 — A required `timeZone` breaks three screens that shipped this morning.

The plan makes the parameter **required** on all three report routes and notes
that "every web reader must be updated in lockstep" — while putting the screens
out of scope, in `REPORTS-4-WEB (CRM-131)`. Between merging this and merging
that, `/reports/queue-by-status`, `/reports/promise-share` and
`/reports/agent-load` all answer 422 to the pages built for them.

The criterion asks for the opposite: *"when a report is read, then the behaviour
is stated in the contract rather than assumed — the document says what the
default is, and the test proves it."* Optional, with the default written down
and tested. The accounts listing settled exactly this shape when it grew a
`state`: existing callers do not change behaviour because a new story needed
something.

### 2 — The window must not be applied to every report. One of them would start lying.

This is the important one, and it is a fault in the **criteria**, which have been
amended (`scripts/criteria/reports.md`, REPORTS-4-API) rather than papered over.

- **Agent load is a snapshot.** Load means *work still on the person* —
  `REPORTS-3-API`'s own criteria say so. Filtered to today, an agent holding five
  week-old tickets has a load of zero. That is not a narrower answer, it is a
  false one. **Agent load takes no window.**
- **Queue by status is a snapshot too.** Filtered to today, `closed: 104`
  becomes `closed: 0` and the report stops answering the question it is named
  for. It may take a window — "raised in this window, by status" is a real
  question — but only if the answer **echoes the window**, so a reader knows
  which of the two questions they are looking at.
- **Promise share is genuinely periodic** and is the natural home for a window:
  which promises finished in it.

The story's own example is about a ticket being *raised* at 01:30 local, so the
`created_at` window on queue-by-status is what carries it.

### 3 — `sla_breaches` has no `recorded_at` column.

The plan says to filter `countBreachedByKind` on "`sla_breaches.recorded_at` or
the column the breach's settled-at is stored on — verify against the schema
before choosing". The column is **`breached_at`**
(`0003__service_levels.sql:27`). A plan whose job is to remove that uncertainty
should not hand it to the builder.

### 4 — The deleted plan's "current behaviour" never existed.

It said *"Current: `today` is whatever `date(created_at)` returns — i.e. the
UTC day"* and adds a regression check: `grep -R "date(created_at)" api/src` must
return no matches. `date(created_at)` appears nowhere in this repository and
never has — no report filters by date at all today. The check would have passed
forever, on any codebase, which is the shape of a check that is read as evidence
and is not one.

### 5 — Naming one edge of an over-long span is unanswerable.

The plan refuses a span above the ceiling with `fields: ['from']` **or**
`['to']`, "whichever names the offending edge". Neither edge is at fault: the
span is. Name both — `unprocessable(['from', 'to'])` — which is also what a
screen needs in order to highlight the thing the reader must change.

### 6 — Deriving midnight needs two passes, and the comment is the point.

`Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` in a `Set` is the right validity check —
cheap, and no exception on the hot path. But the boundary itself cannot be
`Date.parse(day + 'T00:00:00Z') - offset` computed once: the offset **at
midnight UTC** on that date is not always the offset **at midnight local** on
that date, and on a DST-change day they differ by an hour.

Compute the offset at a first guess, shift, then recompute at the shifted
instant and shift again. It converges in two, and the comment must say why —
otherwise the second pass looks like superstition and the next reader deletes it.

### 7 — Say what the window means in the answer, not only in the document.

Every report that takes one returns the window it used, as the two UTC instants
plus the zone it was asked in. `queue-by-status` already echoes nothing;
`/accounts` echoes its `state` for exactly this reason. A number whose period is
only knowable from the request that produced it cannot be checked, quoted, or
put in a screenshot.

## Story Goal

The three admin reports (`queue-by-status`, `promise-share`, `agent-load`) count rows against a **day boundary derived in the reader's IANA time zone**, not in UTC. A single window helper lives in the reports feature and is called by every report route — one implementation, one refusal path for an unknown zone, one place that says what "today" means.

Concrete outcome: a caller at UTC+3 who asks `/reports/queue-by-status?timeZone=Africa/Cairo` at 01:30 local time sees a ticket stored `22:30Z` on the previous UTC day counted as **today**. The mirror at UTC−5 does the opposite. An unknown zone answers **422 VALIDATION_FAILED** naming `timeZone` — never a silent fall back to UTC.

**Explicitly not in scope**

- Per-user zone preferences, or a column to store one. The zone travels with the request.
- Working hours / calendar. S-3: clocks run 24/7.
- Changes to storage (still UTC — every stamp `new Date(now() * 1000).toISOString()`) or display (already handled by `web/src/shared/i18n/format.ts:20–27`).
- The screen — that is `REPORTS-4-WEB (CRM-131)`.
- Any date library. `Intl` is in the Node 26 runtime.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the three reports count every live row regardless of when it was created; there is no time filter and no zone.
- **New behaviour:** every report route takes a **required** `timeZone` (IANA identifier) plus **optional** `from` / `to` (ISO calendar dates `YYYY-MM-DD` interpreted in that zone). Missing `from`/`to` means "today in that zone". The window is exclusive on the upper bound (`start ≤ x < end`). Storage remains UTC; the window is UTC ISO strings computed from the zone-local day. An unknown or malformed zone is **422 VALIDATION_FAILED** with `fields: ['timeZone']`. A span greater than the ceiling (see below) is **422** with `fields: ['from']` or `['to']` — whichever names the offending edge.
- **Contract for "no `timeZone` given":** the parameter is **required**. Missing = 422 with `fields: ['timeZone']`. Documented in `openapi.json`. There is no silent UTC fall-back.

## Implementation Tasks

### 1 — Create the window helper

**Create file:** `api/src/features/reports/reports.window.js`

Add a small module owned by the reports feature. It resolves the report window from an Express `req` and a `now` clock. It is the only place the zone-to-UTC-day boundary is computed.

Requirements:

- Export a constant `MAX_WINDOW_DAYS = 92` — BR-4 applied to an aggregate. Comment explains why 92: a quarter is the longest range an admin reads on one page.
- Export `KNOWN_TIME_ZONES` — `new Set(Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone'))`. One Set, built at module load, so an unknown zone is a `has()` check, not a `try/catch` on `formatToParts`. Comment cites `scripts/rules.txt` line 28 (E-2): a report answering the wrong day is worse than one refusing.
- Export `resolveReportWindow(req, { now })`. Signature returns `{ startUtcIso, endUtcIso, timeZone }` on success, or throws `unprocessable([field])`. Behaviour:
  1. Read `req.query?.timeZone`. If missing/empty/non-string → `throw unprocessable(['timeZone'])`.
  2. If `!KNOWN_TIME_ZONES.has(timeZone)` → `throw unprocessable(['timeZone'])`.
  3. Read `req.query?.from` and `req.query?.to`. Each, if present, must match `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/`; otherwise `throw unprocessable(['from'])` / `['to']`.
  4. Compute the zone-local calendar date **for `now()`** using `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone, year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit' }).formatToParts(new Date(now() * 1000))`. `en-CA` gives ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` parts, which is why the intake calls it out.
  5. If `from` is absent, default to that local date. If `to` is absent, default to `from + 1 day` (exclusive upper bound; a one-day window = "today").
  6. If `from > to` → `throw unprocessable(['to'])`. If the span in calendar days exceeds `MAX_WINDOW_DAYS` → `throw unprocessable(['to'])`.
  7. Convert each local date `YYYY-MM-DD` at `00:00:00` in `timeZone` into a UTC ISO stamp by locating the UTC instant whose zone-local wall clock equals that midnight. Implement this without a library: build a candidate `Date.UTC(y, m-1, d)` then adjust by the offset that the zone reports for that instant via `formatToParts(candidate)` — one round-trip is enough because the offset is stable at midnight for any zone this story cares about (an ambiguous DST midnight resolves to the earlier instant; document the choice in a comment).
  8. Return `{ startUtcIso, endUtcIso, timeZone }` — both stamps ending `.000Z` to match how storage writes them (`new Date(now() * 1000).toISOString()`).

Add a header comment that says exactly what the intake says: **the zone moves the boundary; it never rewrites a row**. Storage stays UTC (BR-3).

**Rationale to include as prose in the module:**

> One implementation, called by every report. A second one is the defect this story exists to prevent — the `promise-share` route computing a boundary the `agent-load` route does not is the shape L-62 named.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing `timeZone`** — trigger: query without `timeZone`. Behaviour: 422 with `fields: ['timeZone']`. Enforced in `reports.window.js` step 1.
- **Unknown `timeZone`** — trigger: `?timeZone=Foo/Bar`. Behaviour: 422 with `fields: ['timeZone']`. Enforced by `KNOWN_TIME_ZONES.has(...)`. Never falls back to UTC.
- **Malformed `from` / `to`** — trigger: `?from=2026/01/01` or `?to=yesterday`. Behaviour: 422 with `fields: ['from']` or `['to']`.
- **Reversed range** — trigger: `from > to`. Behaviour: 422 with `fields: ['to']`.
- **Span greater than `MAX_WINDOW_DAYS`** — trigger: 93+ calendar days. Behaviour: 422 with `fields: ['to']`. BR-4 on an aggregate.
- **UTC+13 reader at 00:30 local time** — trigger: a ticket stored `11:30Z` on the previous UTC day, admin at `Pacific/Auckland` (DST) asks for today. Expected: ticket is counted. Enforced by `resolveReportWindow` computing the zone-local calendar date via `formatToParts` before conversion.
- **UTC−10 reader at 23:00 local time** — trigger: a ticket stored `08:00Z` on the following UTC day. Expected: ticket is **not** counted (still tomorrow morning UTC, but yesterday-into-today evening local).
- **DST forward jump at local midnight** — trigger: a zone whose midnight does not exist on the transition day (rare; noted for completeness). Behaviour: resolve to the earlier valid instant. Documented in a comment inside `reports.window.js`.
- **Non-admin caller** — trigger: agent token. Behaviour: 403 FORBIDDEN from `adminOnly` middleware before the window helper runs (`reports.routes.js:12`). No change from today.
- **A soft-deleted ticket in the window** — behaviour unchanged: `deleted_at IS NULL` still filters it out at every query (see comment at `reports.repository.js:9-11`).
- **Ambiguous "today" when `now` moves during a request** — trigger: request starts at 23:59:59, the reader's midnight boundary passes mid-request. Behaviour: `now()` is called once at the top of `resolveReportWindow` and reused; a request answers the boundary that was true when it entered.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Not a schema migration.** No table change; no new column. The window is a request-scoped value; storage remains UTC.
- **Contract change.** Adding a required `timeZone` parameter is a breaking change for any existing consumer. Every web reader (`REPORTS-*-WEB`) must ship the parameter in the same release; coordinate with those stories' owners (listed in Prerequisites).
- **Rollback on failure.** Revert four source files (`reports.window.js`, `reports.routes.js`, `reports.read.js`, `reports.repository.js`), the `index.js` export, the `compose.js` wiring, and the openapi entries. No data written by this story means no data to un-write. Half-applied state: if the routes require `timeZone` but a stale web build still calls without it, every report answers 422 with `fields: ['timeZone']` — visible, refused, not silently wrong.

4. **Contract check:** `cd api && npm test -- openapi-contract.test.js` — every reports path documents `422` and the three query parameters.
5. **Application boots:** `cd api && npm start` then `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin>" 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/reports/queue-by-status'` returns 422 `{"code":"VALIDATION_FAILED","fields":["timeZone"],...}`; the same URL with `?timeZone=UTC` returns the six-key `counts` object.
6. **No AI attribution:** `git grep -inE "(claude|copilot|chatgpt|assistant|ai[- ]generated|generated by ai)" -- . ':!.squad'` returns nothing.
7. **Architecture check:** `cd api && node ../scripts/verify-architecture.mjs` — no new cross-feature reach; the window helper lives inside `features/reports/` and is exported through `features/reports/index.js`.

## Done Criteria

- [x] A ticket stored `22:30Z` on 2 September is in a Cairo reader's today, whose window runs `21:00Z` on the 2nd to `21:00Z` on the 3rd — the concrete case the story exists for, and the one `date(created_at)` gets wrong.
- [x] The mirror holds: the same instant is in a New York reader's today too, on a different calendar day and a different pair of instants.
- [x] The window is optional (review item 1). With none, every report answers exactly what it answered before the parameter existed, so the three screens shipped this morning keep working.
- [x] An unknown zone is 422 naming `timeZone`, never a quiet fall back to UTC. A range with no zone to read it in is refused for the same reason.
- [x] A span longer than 92 days names **both** edges (review item 5): the span is what is wrong, and a screen highlighting one of the two would point at the wrong control.
- [x] Storage is untouched. The zone moves the boundary; no row is rewritten, and no column stores an offset — an offset is not a zone, because a zone changes offset twice a year.
- [x] **The load report takes no window** (review item 2, and the criteria were amended to say so). Filtered to a day it would report an agent holding five week-old tickets as idle.
- [x] Queue-by-status echoes the window it used, or null. Its answer means one of two different things and the request is not where a reader should have to look for which.
- [x] The promise report measures the window against when a promise **finished** — a clock that stopped or a breach that was recorded — not when the ticket was raised. Proved by moving only `stopped_at`.
- [x] `sla_breaches.breached_at`, not the `recorded_at` the plan guessed at (review item 3).
- [x] Documented in `api/openapi.json`, prose, including what no window means and why agent-load has none.
- [x] `cd api && npm test` — 617 pass. `cd web` — 380 pass, build clean. Six guards green.
- [x] No AI-attribution strings in the diff.

## What the mutation pass proved — and the two bugs the tests found first

| # | what was broken | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | one pass at the boundary instead of two | 1 fail |
| W2 | the far edge is `start + 24 hours` | 1 fail |
| W3 | an unknown zone falls back to no window | 1 fail |
| W4 | the span ceiling is removed | 1 fail |
| W5 | the window never reaches the query | 4 fail |

**W1 passed at first**, and that was the honest signal: the second pass was
unpinned. It only differs when a zone changes offset between midnight UTC and
midnight local — so a test was written for New Zealand leaving daylight time on
5 April 2026, where one pass lands an hour late and the local day is 25 hours
long. With that test, W1 fails.

**Two real defects were found by the tests, not by the review** — see L-69:

- `end = startOfLocalDay(to) + DAY_MS`, written ten lines below a comment
  explaining why a fixed 24 hours is wrong at the other end of the same
  function.
- `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` does not contain `UTC`, so the most
  obvious zone anybody would send answered 422. The plan that was deleted said
  to use a `try/catch` on `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instead and was right; the
  review kept the `Set` for being cleaner.
